LESSON: LINES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: GEOMETRY
Topic 3.1: Lines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Lines, part of GEOMETRY in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why is line construction skill important? 2. How can you construct a line?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Lines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: Active and communication skills as learners in pairs or groups / individually bisect

lines by construction.

● Communication and Collaboration: as learners develop signing and observing skills as they collaboratively work

to come up with different types of lines.

50

Values:
Responsibility: as learners in pairs or groups or as individuals share digital devices and other resources to draw parallel

lines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: as learners observe internet safety and security by accessing safe online mathematical sites to learn

more on lines.

Link to other subjects;

Creative arts: learners relate interaction with various lines in the environment and appreciate use of parallel, vertical

and perpendicular lines in daily life to knowledge in Creative Arts.

Suggested assessment method: Written exercise, signed work, Observation and Group discussions.

Suggested learning resources:

● Chalkboard ruler

● 30cm ruler

● straight edges

● Signs dictionary
